answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can transact. To forge a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand bonds, and any identity caught duplicating work or colluding loses its stake, so the attack price scales linearly with its size. Reputation threads through that stake: honest history lifts an agent toward the zenith of trust, while a fresh identity starts at zero and must earn its way up. The cost is real capital at risk, not just compute.
